events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.92)
events.body:
This is a rider-side cancellation on an instant (on-demand) RydeX booking, so the fee can only arise through NS-0's rider branch, which sends the case to NS-4 [F2][NS-0]. The timeline is the controlling record: acceptance at 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 2 min 55 s (175 s) after matching, which is inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no cancellation fee is chargeable [F2][NS-4]. The system trace confirms this element (175 s is not "more than 3 min") and permits refund_full with quantum equal to the fee charged [F2][F5][NS-4].

The alternative route by which a rider-cancellation fee could stand — a rider no-show under NS-1 — was never triggered on these facts. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" [F4], the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at null) [F3], and GPS shows his closest approach to the pickup was 1685 m, outside the 200 m arrival radius, at the moment of cancellation [F1]. NS-1 requires all three of (i) the "I'm Here" tap, (ii) GPS position at the pickup point, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting there; each fails here, so the fee cannot be sustained and NS-2 requires full return of the $6.61 [F1][F3][F4][F5][NS-1][NS-2]. The driver's own chat "about 5 min, traffic" and his statement that he "was on my way" describe him still en route, not the rider failing to appear, and the system records override those statements in any event [F8][F9][F1][NS-1].

The driver's traffic explanation does not change the outcome. The only congestion record is a band-3 (20–29 km/h) section on NASSIM ROAD [F10], which under RD-4(b) is not a severe-congestion band and in any case is irrelevant because the fee fails on the timing and no-show preconditions, not on any duty to reach the pickup in time; no incidents were logged near the route and weather was fair [F10][F11][F12][NS-4]. Quantum therefore follows NS-4 with the fare record: the amount charged was $6.61 and the full amount is refundable, disbursed as a voucher under NS-7 [F2][F5][NS-7].

On the proposed account flag: NS-2's flag is attached specifically to a driver pressing "I'm Here" while GPS shows him outside the pickup range — that never happened here (F4 shows no tap at all), so NS-2's flag condition is not met [F4][NS-2]. The driver's profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days [F14], but RD-6's flag is tied to this case being established as a route-deviation breach with refund > 0 (or a recorded RD-1 violation), which this no-show case is not, and profile facts cannot alone decide or escalate the matter [F14][RD-6]. The trace also reports no flag required, so no account action is taken.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 rider-cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag needed on this file.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's framing that the $6.61 is 'refundable in full under NS-2 with NS-3' is rejected as to NS-3: NS-3 governs a driver-initiated cancellation, whereas the record shows cancelled_by = rider [F2][NS-0], so NS-3 is inapplicable and the correct basis for the refund is NS-4 (rider cancelled within 3 minutes) with NS-2's return of a fee collected without the NS-1 preconditions [F2][F1][F4][NS-4][NS-2].

RIDER: You were charged a $6.61 cancellation fee after you cancelled your RydeX ride. We've reviewed the timing: you cancelled about 2 minutes 55 seconds after a driver accepted, which is inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the fee should not have applied. We're refunding the full $6.61 to you as a Ryde voucher. Nothing is needed from you, and no account action is being taken against you.

DRIVER: The $6.61 cancellation fee from this trip is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The rider cancelled about 2 minutes 55 seconds after you accepted, inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the fee could not stand. The no-show rule also didn't apply: there was no "I'm Here" tap, no record of you at the pickup point, and GPS showed you about 1685 m away. No account flag or other action is being taken against you on this case.

ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider-side cancellation on an instant (on-demand) RydeX booking, so the fee can only arise through NS-0's rider branch, which sends the case to NS-4 [F2][NS-0]. The system trace confirms this element (175 s is not "more than 3 min") and permits refund_full with quantum equal to the fee charged [F2][F5][NS-4].

The alternative route by which a rider-cancellation fee could stand — a rider no-show under NS-1 — was never triggered on these facts. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" [F4], the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at null) [F3], and GPS shows his closest approach to the pickup was 1685 m, outside the 200 m arrival radius, at the moment of cancellation [F1]. NS-1 requires all three of (i) the "I'm Here" tap, (ii) GPS position at the pickup point, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting there; each fails here, so the fee cannot be sustained and NS-2 requires full return of the $6.61 [F1][F3][F4][F5][NS-1][NS-2]. The driver's own chat "about 5 min, traffic" and his statement that he "was on my way" describe him still en route, not the rider failing to appear, and the system records override those statements in any event [F8][F9][F1][NS-1].

The driver's traffic explanation does not change the outcome. The only congestion record is a band-3 (20–29 km/h) section on NASSIM ROAD [F10], which under RD-4(b) is not a severe-congestion band and in any case is irrelevant because the fee fails on the timing and no-show preconditions, not on any duty to reach the pickup in time; no incidents were logged near the route and weather was fair [F10][F11][F12][NS-4]. certificate: ✗ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 175 s after acceptance (F2)
allowed outcomes: refund_full; amount = cancellation fee $6.61

claims.assertion: This is an on-demand booking cancelled by the rider 2 min 55 s after acceptance — within the 3-minute free-cancellation window — so no cancellation fee is chargeable.
The driver never came within 200 m of the pickup point (closest approach 1685 m at 14:07:55) and driver_arrived_at is null, so the driver was nowhere near the pickup when the rider cancelled.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here", so the pickup-waiting precondition for any rider-side cancellation fee is absent.
Because the driver did not press "I'm Here" and never entered the pickup range, none of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is satisfied and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full.

The driver's own message at 14:06 said he was still about 5 minutes away in traffic, corroborating that he had not arrived; the GPS record (F1/F3) controls over his later statement that he "was on my way".

No incident or severe congestion is recorded on the route during the trip window (fair weather, only a moderate band-3 section), so the driver's "traffic" excuse does not excuse his failure to reach the pickup point.
The refund amounts to the full fee charged of $6.61, per the fare record, chargeable as a Ryde voucher within 30 days of the trip.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days, which supports sending his account for review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The rider is the cancelling party, and NS-4 makes a rider cancellation fee valid only for cancellations after 3 minutes; the borderline timing (2 min 55 s vs 3:00, F2) is the whole case and the other side will argue the record shows a fee was levied, implying the platform treated it as chargeable.

The driver's chat message (F8) says he was ~5 minutes away, which the driver may use to argue he was progressing normally and that the rider cancelled prematurely rather than that he breached any duty to arrive.
The rider-side profile shows 1 prior dispute in 90 days (0 upheld) (F13), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of fee disputes, though it cannot decide this case.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after acceptance, i.e. within the 3-minute window measured from matching, so under the instant-booking rule the $6.61 fee is not chargeable and falls to be refunded.
The driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and the platform never recorded him arriving at the pickup point, so the rider-no-show branch that could have justified the fee was never triggered.

GPS shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 1685 m and he never entered the 200 m arrival radius, so the NS-1 (ii) location requirement — the only route by which a no-show cancellation fee can stand — is not met.

The driver's own statement that he was 'on his way' and his chat estimate of 'about 5 min' confirm he had not reached the pickup point when the rider cancelled; his statement does not assert the rider failed to show up.
The charge of $6.61 is therefore a cancellation fee collected without any NS-1 condition being satisfied, and is refundable in full as recorded on the fare record.

No traffic or weather condition excuses the failure to reach the pickup point: no incidents were recorded near the route and weather was fair with no rain, and the only congestion record is a moderate band 3 (20–29 km/h) on NASSIM ROAD, which is not a severe-congestion band and does not cover the unmet NS-1 requirement.

The driver has 2 no-show disputes upheld in the last 90 days against 666 trips, which under the repeated-breach account-review ground supports an additional flag_account referral alongside the refund (offered as an additional action only, not as the basis of the finding).

weaknesses: F8 and F9 (driver's chat 'about 5 min, traffic' and his statement 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled') show the driver accepted the job and was moving toward the pickup, and the rider-side fairness rule that a driver late versus ETA gives free cancellation is not in Ryde's policy (NS-8 is informational only and the file has no ETA field), so the driver cannot lean on the rider's stated reason of 'driver was nowhere near'.

F10 shows a speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) record on NASSIM ROAD during 14:00–14:12, which the rider may cite as corroboration that the driver was delayed and unreachable in time even though the GPS record (F1) shows he was 1685 m away.
The rider filed within the dispute window and their own profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days (F13), so there is no credibility discount available against the rider's account.

points.response: Concede — the opponent accepts the timing: rider cancellation at 2 min 55 s (F2) is inside the 3-minute window, so the fee is not chargeable under NS-4 with NS-0.
Concede, and this is the core of my case: driver_arrived_at is null (F3) and no 'I'm Here' tap exists (F4), so the NS-1 branch that could have justified the fee was never triggered.
Concede on the location requirement: the closest approach was 1685 m (F1), so NS-1 (ii) fails on the GPS record, not on argument.

Concede the opponent's reading of F8/F9: 'about 5 min, traffic' (F8) and 'I was on my way' (F9) confirm the driver never reached the pickup point and neither statement alleges the rider failed to show up, so NS-3 applies against the fee.
Concede: with every NS-1 condition unmet, the $6.61 taken at 14:07:55 (F5, F2) is refundable in full under NS-2 with NS-3.

Concede that the traffic record cannot save the fee: only band 3 on NASSIM ROAD (F10), no incidents near the route (F11) and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F12) leave the unmet NS-1 requirement unexplained.
Concede the flag_account referral on the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F14), offered only as an additional action to the refund, consistent with my C8.

Conceded as to the legal test but not as to the driver's conduct: the timeline (F2) records cancellation 2 min 55 s after acceptance, and NS-4 makes riders chargeable only beyond 3 minutes, so the fee is refundable — my brief already asks for exactly this outcome.

Accepted on the facts: GPS puts the driver's closest approach at 1685 m with driver_arrived_at null (F1, F3); the driver's case does not rest on denying the distance, and no clause penalises the distance itself now that the fee falls away under NS-4.
Accepted: the timeline shows the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (F4), so the NS-1 waiting precondition was never met and the rider's $6.61 cannot stand on NS-1.
No contest — with the location and "I'm Here" requirements unmet (F1, F4) the charge on record (F5) is returned in full under NS-2, which is precisely the outcome the driver's brief requests.

The rider's own corroboration cuts the other way: F8 shows the driver replying within a minute of acceptance and still en route (F9), which is normal progress under a fixed-fare RydeX booking, not a breach of any duty; NS-4 fixes liability by elapsed time (F2) regardless of the driver's position.

The driver does not need a traffic excuse once the fee fails on timing (F2) and on the unmet NS-1 preconditions (F1, F4); the moderate band-3 record on NASSIM ROAD and the fair weather (F10, F12) are noted only as context, and no incident was reported (F11).
Agreed on quantum: the fare record shows $6.61 charged (F5), and the driver joins the request that it be refunded in full, dispatched in the voucher form specified for fee refunds.

Partial contest: NS-2's account-review referral is attached to the "I'm Here"-while-outside-range scenario, whereas J14 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes over 666 trips in 90 days; the 2 upheld findings alone do not make F14 a repeated-breach record sufficient for an account flag, and the driver opposes any flag on this file.
